compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The sibling admission runner fills fixture coverage once, at a single point in time. Two
things then reopen gaps: a criterion added to the registry later starts life with no
fixture, and a criterion whose candidates all failed to reproduce is left with none. Without
a mechanism that revisits those gaps, coverage decays from its first day and the only repair
is someone noticing.

A repair loop that spends money unattended is itself a hazard, so the loop needs a bound
that does not depend on anyone watching it.

## Approach

A gap-only repair loop that converges and then costs nothing.

**Gap-only scope.** Each run considers only criteria that
`criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')` reports and for which no spec file
exists under `.rebar/evals/` or `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`. Criteria that already have a
fixture are never revisited, so the loop's work shrinks monotonically as coverage completes
and reaches zero when every criterion is covered. This is what makes unattended spend
bounded by construction rather than by a watchdog.

**Circuit breaker.** The loop records, per criterion, how many consecutive runs failed to
yield an admitted fixture. A run counts as a failure for that criterion in either of two
ways: the emitted spec's candidates failed to reproduce, or no spec was emitted at all
because the criterion was reported `skipped-unbalanced` (it could not supply a case on both
sides of the fire/no-fire axis). On the third such run it creates a ticket titled
exactly `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>` — the literal prefix `unreliable-criterion: `
followed by the registry criterion id, with no other text in the title — and stops
attempting that criterion. The sibling selector already skips a criterion carrying an open
ticket with that title, so the pair forms the breaker: while the ticket is open the criterion
costs nothing, and closing it after a rubric fix lets the criterion re-enter mining on the
next run.

**Portability.** Recurring work must not depend on a CI provider. The trigger is
operation-linked with an in-process due-stamp: the loop records its last run in the
repository's rebar state, and a rebar plan-review operation in the repository advances it
when the configured interval has elapsed, defaulting to 30 days. It is also directly
invocable as a command, so an operator, a cron, or any CI provider can drive it, and a
project with no CI provider still converges through ordinary gate usage alone. No step
depends on a POSIX-only shell or on a `.rebar/` path resolved from the process working
directory.

**Unattended spend bound.** Mining is free, so only admission costs. Each run pre-flights
through `ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=25.0)` against the loop's own ledger file and stops when
the run's remaining headroom cannot cover the next criterion, leaving the rest for the next
interval. That bounds unattended spend to $25 per interval regardless of how many gaps exist.

**Failure disposition.** A transient model or transport error inside a criterion's admission
attempt is RETRYABLE and retried within the run. `BudgetExceeded` is FATAL for the run and
non-retryable: the run stops with completed criteria admitted and their spend reconciled, and
the next interval resumes. A criterion whose candidates fail to reproduce is not an error at
all — it increments the breaker counter and the run continues to the next criterion. When a
transient failure and the ceiling coincide, the ceiling wins and the run stops.

## Scope

The loop command, its due-stamp trigger and interval configuration, the per-criterion
consecutive-failure counter, the `unreliable-criterion:` ticket creation, and the loop's own
ledger file. It reuses the sibling selector, emitter and admission runner rather than
duplicating any of them.

## Non-goals

- Repairing a criterion recorded as unreliable; that is the work the filed ticket represents.
- Revisiting criteria that already have a fixture.
- Removing or rewriting an existing fixture.
- Any human curation step between mining and admission.

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive: a new command, a new state stamp, and a new ledger file. No existing command,
spec, or persisted format changes. Back-out is deleting the command and its stamp; the
stamp is the only new persisted state and nothing reads it if the command is absent, so
removal leaves the repository in its prior state with no data loss.

## Testing

Unit tests drive the breaker counter, the gap-only selection, the due-stamp interval
arithmetic and the ledger stop condition with a stubbed admission runner, so each assertion
is deterministic without a model. A subprocess test covers the command with no CI
environment present. Ticket creation is exercised against a temporary store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A criterion that already has a spec file is absent from a run's attempt list; verified
      by `pytest` asserting the selected id set excludes it.
- [ ] The third consecutive failed run creates exactly one ticket whose title equals
      `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>`, and the first and second do not; verified by
      `pytest` against a temporary store asserting the title string and the ticket count
      after each run.
- [ ] A run in which the criterion is reported `skipped-unbalanced` increments the same
      counter as a reproduction failure; verified by `pytest` asserting the ticket is created
      after three runs of mixed failure kinds.
- [ ] A criterion with an open ticket of that title is absent from the attempt list; verified
      by `pytest` asserting the id is not selected.
- [ ] A run stops before attempting a criterion whose estimate exceeds the run's remaining
      headroom, and admits the criteria it completed; verified by `pytest` against the real
      `ledger.reserve` with `cap_usd=25.0`, asserting the admitted set and that the ledger
      total is at most 25.0.
- [ ] The command runs with no CI environment variables set and reports its attempt list;
      verified by a `pytest` subprocess test with a cleared environment.
- [ ] The due-stamp advances only after the configured interval has elapsed; verified by
      `pytest` asserting no attempt occurs at interval minus one day and one occurs at the
      interval.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; a run over a store with a seeded gap
attempts exactly that gap; a seeded three-failure history produces the ticket and the skip.

## Budget

**Hard cap $100** for building this child and its first runs. Each unattended run is
separately capped at $25 by its own pre-flight, and the loop's total cost falls to zero once
every criterion is covered or recorded as unreliable.

file_impact.reason: The gap-only loop: attempt selection, the consecutive-failure counter, the unreliable-criterion ticket creation and the per-run budget stop.
Expose the loop as a directly invocable command so an operator, a cron or any CI provider can drive it.
Add the loop's interval setting, defaulting to 30 days.
Unit tests for gap-only selection, the three-strike breaker and its ticket title, the skip on an open ticket, the per-run ledger stop and the due-stamp interval.

compiled_state.title: Gap-only self-healing fixture loop with an unreliable-criterion circuit breaker
